title: Reducedness after extension to two perfect scalar fields
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $E/k$, $F/k$ be field extensions [def-pc-field-extension]. Suppose $E$ and $F$ are perfect: each has characteristic zero, or has characteristic $p>0$ and surjective map $x\mapsto x^p$. Let $A$ be any commutative $k$-algebra, not necessarily reduced, finitely generated or nonzero. Using tensor products of commutative algebras with multiplication $(a\otimes e)(b\otimes e')=ab\otimes ee'$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], one has $$A\otimes_kE\text{ is reduced}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\otimes_kF\text{ is reduced}.$$ Here a ring is reduced if every element $x$ with $x^n=0$ for some integer $n\ge1$ is zero. No embedding between $E$ and $F$, algebraicity over $k$, or perfectness of $k$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00I4 (lemma-perfect-reduced), applied over each of E and F, combined with fields.tex Tag 0H7K (lemma-common-extension-field); tensor cancellation and descent of nilpotents implement the comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] to choose a field $M$ and $k$-embeddings $i_E:E\to M$, $i_F:F\to M$. For $D=E,F$, use $i_D$ as the $D$-algebra structure of $M$, so the composite $k\to D\to M$ is the chosen structure map $k\to M$. Put $B_D=A\otimes_kD$ and $T=A\otimes_kM$.

For each $D=E,F$, cancellation [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change], with $R=k$, $S=D$, its algebra $A=M$ and its algebra $B$ equal to our $A$, gives $M\otimes_D(D\otimes_kA)\simeq M\otimes_kA$. Flip the tensor factors to obtain a ring isomorphism $\theta_D:B_D\otimes_DM\simeq T$, with $\theta_D((a\otimes d)\otimes m)=a\otimes i_D(d)m$ and inverse $a\otimes m\mapsto(a\otimes1)\otimes m$. Here the flips are induced by the bilinear map $(x,y)\mapsto y\otimes x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; their squares fix each pure tensor, and they preserve products because $(y\otimes x)(y'\otimes x')=yy'\otimes xx'$. The ring structures and pure-tensor multiplication are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Thus these flips and the cancellation give precisely the displayed ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule), in the cancellation form stated by the cited node; flips checked on pure tensors.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-field-extension-tensor-injective] over the field $D$, to its field extension $M/D$ and its commutative algebra $B_D$. It gives an injective map $B_D\to B_D\otimes_DM$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Composing with $\theta_D$ gives an injective ring map $j_D:B_D\to T$ satisfying $j_D(a\otimes d)=a\otimes i_D(d)$. This applies without requiring that $B_D$ be nonzero or reduced.

source.place: Scalar-extension injectivity in the cited Mathlib leaf; composition with the isomorphism of step 2.

proof.text: Assume $B_E$ is reduced. Since $E$ is perfect and $M$ is a field, hence reduced (a nonzero element is a unit and no power of a unit is zero), [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-reduced-tensor] over $E$ implies that $B_E\otimes_EM$ is reduced. The isomorphism $\theta_E$ makes $T$ reduced: if $t^n=0$, then $(\theta_E^{-1}(t))^n=0$, so $\theta_E^{-1}(t)=0$ and $t=0$.

source.place: Tag 00I4 (lemma-perfect-reduced), applied over E; preservation under a ring isomorphism checked explicitly.

proof.text: If $x\in B_F$ satisfies $x^n=0$ with $n\ge1$, then $j_F(x)^n=j_F(x^n)=0$ in the reduced ring $T$. Hence $j_F(x)=0=j_F(0)$, and the injectivity from step 3 implies $x=0$. Thus $B_F$ is reduced. Conversely assume $B_F$ is reduced and apply [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-reduced-tensor] over the perfect field $F$ to $B_F$ and the reduced field $M$. This makes $B_F\otimes_FM$, and therefore $T$ via $\theta_F$, reduced. For any nilpotent $x\in B_E$, the same equation $j_E(x)^n=0$ and injectivity of $j_E$ give $x=0$. This proves both implications.

source.place: Tag 00I4 (lemma-perfect-reduced), applied over F; both nilpotent-descent arguments written out.
